lower_bound.quote: Since $|E|<|V|$, the multigraph $G$ contains no cycle and no loop: a cycle or a loop through $v$ vertices already uses at least $v$ edges, so a graph containing one would have at least as many edges as vertices, forcing $|E|\ge|V|$ — impossible.
lower_bound.witness: COUNTEREXAMPLE. The inference is a non-sequitur and the conclusion is false in an instance the proof must cover. A cycle/loop on v vertices forces |E| >= v, not |E| >= |V|; isolated or lightly-used vertices make |E| < |V| compatible with a loop. Concrete instance: n=1, u=1/3, geometric pieces q_1=2/3 (vertex 1), q_0=1/3 (vertex 0). Xiang Yu uses K=1 cut, splitting the piece 2/3 into 1/3+1/3. Then A={1/3,1/3,1/3}, M=3, |E|=floor(3/2)=1 < 2=|V|. Ties are broken 'arbitrarily' per the text, so we may set a_1,a_2 to be the two halves of piece 1 and a_3=q_0. The single pair P_1={a_1,a_2} then has both parts inside piece 1, i.e. G has a loop at vertex 1 — contradicting the quoted conclusion. Moreover the component containing vertex n=1 is this loop, so it is not a simple tree and admits no proper 2-colouring, so the rest of the proof (choice of signs s, and the assertion that the two endpoints of each pair are distinct pieces) is unavailable for this tie-breaking.
lower_bound.load_bearing: The whole lower-bound proof rests on T being a loop-free tree: the proper 2-colouring producing the signed subset sum Xi, and the identification of each edge's contribution with epsilon_i = |a_{2i-1}-a_{2i}|, both fail if the component containing vertex n contains a loop or cycle.

parsed.notes: Answer c=2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) correct. Reduction (Lemma 2) and upper bound (subset-sum gap plus overlay/cross-pairing, mark count m-1<=n) check out. Lower bound's acyclicity step is a genuine non-sequitur, refutable already at n=1 under the text's own arbitrary tie-breaking.
